text:
maia: Heads up — seeing repeated scale-down <-> scale-up churn on GPU nodepools in eu-west-2 over the last 3 hours. Seems correlated with intermittent network egress errors to our image registry and a couple of spot interruptions.

devon: Ugh. Any CA logs or flags to look at?

maia: Pasted the relevant flags we rolled out this morning:
```
--expander=least-waste
--scale-down-unneeded-time=2m
--scale-down-delay=1m
--max-node-provision-time=15m
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
```

maia: When the registry egress fails briefly, pods stay Pending for ~30s, CA sees them as fit->unfit and nukes nodes, then we reprovision GPUs and the cycle repeats.

kumar: Hmm. `least-waste` + low `scale-down-unneeded-time` seems risky with flaky networking. Could flip to `most-pods` or add a longer unneeded/ delay to avoid reacting to transient failures.

liam: Also consider `--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5` (higher threshold) so lightly-utilized GPU nodes aren't removed during short disruptions.

devon: Agree. Another idea: add health check gating for image pull errors so CA treats pull/fetch failures differently from real resource pressure. Currently we interpret Pending as schedulable.

maia: Good call. Also noticed spot churn spike in the same window. Cost team pushed more spot instances in that AZ to save money. Might be a compounding factor.

kumar: If spots are the noise source, we should create a small reserved GPU pool (no scale-down) for latency-critical routes and let autoscaler handle best-effort workloads on spots.

ops-bot: [alert] autoscaler: scale_down 3 nodes in eu-west-2/gpu-pool-a at 2026-03-17T14:12:31Z :reason=unneeded

liam: Also thinking about cross-AZ coordination: when one AZ has transient network issues, the expander and balance flags can cause oscillation as CA shifts capacity. We can add `--expendersim-quiet-period` (not a real flag, but you get the idea) — actually we should stagger scale-down across AZs by increasing `--scale-down-delay-after-delete` per nodegroup.

maia: For quick mitigation I propose: 1) rollback to `most-pods`, 2) set `--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m`, 3) provision 2 reserved GPU nodes with `kubelet: no_scale_down=true` taint for critical workloads.

devon: I'm happy to ship those changes. Will open a short PR: `infra/cluster-autoscaler: revert expander, raise delays, add reserved gpu pool` and include rollout plan with a canary in eu-west-2a only.

kumar: Add a note to cost owners: we'll absorb small monthly cost for reserved nodes to prevent user-facing latency/regressions.

liam: After canary, let's run a sim with our expander simulator to validate oscillation metrics before fleet rollout.

maia: Thanks — appreciate the quick triage. Will post logs + sample CA snapshot in the PR description. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: [deploy] PR #3421 merged to canary cluster eu-west-2a :shipit:

devon: Can monitor for 30m then decide. If stable, roll to remaining AZs.

maia: Copy. Observability dashboards will show reduced scale events if this works.

liam: FYI we should follow up with a longer-term fix: smarter CA policy that treats transient image-pull/backoff as a distinct signal from node underutilization. Filing an RFC next week. :memo:
